blocks.features: Four-row reference table of sample letter/number print page identifiers; the guide itself renders this as a combined print+braille table (braille given verbatim below, not a real formatted 40-cell page).

braille.notes: Not a real 40-cell braille page: this is the guide's own reference table pairing each print identifier with its 'Combined Page Numbers' and 'Combined/Continued Numbers' braille renderings (three braille strings per row, in row-major Print/Combined/Combined-Continued order). width recorded as null since this is a table, not a measured braille page.

uncertain: The en dash in 'I–65' is reproduced exactly as it appears in the source (not a hyphen).
resolution: Both runs agree on every value once B's table-column split (print label vs. its two braille forms) is used -- A instead kept the whole row as one literal braille.lines string; B's structured headers/rows is closer to this section's own table schema and was adopted. This is a reference table (print label + its own braille rendering given side by side by the guide itself), not a real 40-cell braille page, so braille.lines is left empty (the runner's own no-braille signal) and the actual braille strings are recorded in braille.notes as evidence instead -- Emboss has no letter/number page-identifier transformation feature in any case (standards-findings.md F-48).
